title: Exploring Efficient Partial Differential Equation Solution Using Speed Galerkin Transformer
problem: FNO-based models for PDE solving have key components that cannot fully leverage GPU hardware potential, limiting applicability to high-resolution and real-time scenarios. Existing implementations achieve suboptimal performance despite strong algorithmic properties.
motivation: Efficient PDE solving is critical for scientific computing and engineering applications requiring real-time inference at high resolution.
method: Speed Galerkin Transformer applies four GPU optimization strategies: (1) multilevel parallel SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK strategy for batched skinny matrix multiplication, (2) memory layout optimization for QKV matrices and positional encodings, (3) multi-head layer normalization fusion, and (4) batched transposition optimization with strided scattering/gathering in 2D FNO. These kernel-level optimizations target bottlenecks specific to Fourier-based transformer operations.
key_novelty: Integrated set of GPU kernel optimizations (SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK, memory layout, layer norm fusion, batched transposition) co-designed specifically for FNO-based Galerkin transformers.
contributions: SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK parallel strategy achieving 10.29x speedup on batched matrix multiplication
Memory layout and multi-head layer normalization fusion achieving 4.41x speedup
Batched transposition optimization with strided operations achieving 2.38x speedup
End-to-end 1.72x speedup on Darcy Flow at 512x512 resolution with 90% parallel efficiency across 8 GPUs
limitations: Evaluation limited to Darcy Flow equation; generalization to other PDE types and comparison with other optimization frameworks not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU kernel optimization for neural PDE solvers
